affected_predicate.description: The poll option originally labeled “Brazil” is replaced with exactly “Canada” and the edit is saved.

competing_trace_defects.description: At step 7, entering “Canada” appends it to the focused option rather than replacing the existing text, producing “BrazilCanada”; the saved poll visibly retains that combined label.
The step-4 attempt does not remove the “USA” option, which remains visible throughout the editor and after the poll is saved.

chains.rationale: The reused claim says Brazil’s options menu was already open, although the target-pre screen shows no such menu. At step 6, the resulting tap merely focuses the Brazil text field and causes no visible defect. The later independent input action appends “Canada,” yielding “BrazilCanada,” and step 8 saves that label; the final visible poll therefore does not show an exact replacement with “Canada.” The reused premise is concurrent with, rather than an observed bridge to, that later editing defect.

summary: The sole strict-MHR reuse target visibly focuses the intended poll-option field without creating or preserving harm. Independent defects are observable: “Canada” is appended to “Brazil,” and “USA” remains present in the saved poll.
